userPrompt: What obligations does a data processor have under GDPR versus a data controller?
responseText:
**Key distinction under GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)**

- **Data Controller**: The entity that determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data (Art. 4(7)). It decides “why” and “how” personal data is processed.
- **Data Processor**: The entity that processes personal data on behalf of the controller (Art. 4(8)). It acts only on documented instructions from the controller.

### Obligations of a Data Controller

The controller carries the primary responsibility and must:

- **Lawful basis & principles** — Ensure every processing activity has a valid legal basis (Art. 6) and complies with all seven principles (Art. 5): lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity & confidentiality, and accountability.
- **Transparency & information duties** — Provide privacy notices to data subjects (Arts. 12–14).
- **Data subject rights** — Facilitate and respond to requests for access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection (Arts. 15–22).
- **Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA)** — Carry out and consult where processing is high-risk (Art. 35–36).
- **Record of processing activities (RoPA)** — Maintain detailed internal records (Art. 30(1)).
- **Security & breach notification** — Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures; notify supervisory authorities of personal data breaches within 72 hours (Art. 33) and, where relevant, communicate to data subjects (Art. 34).
- **Contracts with processors** — Conclude binding data processing agreements (Art. 28(3)) that meet minimum GDPR clauses.
- **Accountability & demonstration** — Be able to prove compliance (Art. 5(2)); appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) where required (Art. 37–39).
- **International transfers** — Ensure adequate safeguards (Chapter V).

The controller is ultimately liable to data subjects and supervisory authorities.

### Obligations of a Data Processor

The processor’s obligations are narrower and flow from the controller’s instructions:

- **Process only on documented instructions** — Including regarding transfers to third countries (Art. 28(3)(a)). Must immediately inform the controller if an instruction infringes GDPR.
- **Ensure confidentiality** — Bind all persons authorised to process the data to confidentiality (Art. 28(3)(b), 32(4)).
- **Security measures** — Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures (Art. 32).
- **Assist the controller** — Help the controller fulfil its obligations regarding:
  - Data subject rights (Art. 28(3)(e))
  - Breach notification (Art. 33)
  - DPIAs and prior consultation (Art. 35–36)
- **Maintain records of processing activities** — Its own RoPA (Art. 30(2)).
- **Sub-processing** — Only engage another processor with the controller’s prior specific or general written authorisation; flow-down the same contractual obligations (Art. 28(2)–(4)).
- **Return or delete data** — At the end of the service, delete or return all personal data unless Union or Member State law requires storage (Art. 28(3)(g)).
- **Demonstrate compliance** — Make all information necessary to demonstrate compliance available to the controller and allow audits/inspections (Art. 28(3)(h)).

A processor becomes a controller (and assumes full controller obligations) if it starts determining the purposes or essential means of processing (Art. 28(10)).

### Summary Table (controller vs processor)

| Obligation                          | Controller | Processor |
|-------------------------------------|------------|-----------|
| Determine purposes & means          | Yes        | No (must follow instructions) |
| Legal basis & Art. 5 principles     | Primary    | Indirect (via instructions) |
| Privacy notices & transparency      | Yes        | No |
| Respond to data subject rights      | Yes        | Assist only |
| DPIA & prior consultation           | Yes        | Assist only |
| Breach notification (SA & DS)       | Yes        | Notify controller without undue delay |
| Data Processing Agreement           | Must conclude & enforce | Must comply with it |
| Records of Processing (RoPA)        | Yes (Art. 30(1)) | Yes (Art. 30(2)) |
| Security measures (Art. 32)         | Yes        | Yes |
| Appoint DPO (if required)           | Yes        | Yes (if criteria met) |
| International transfers safeguards  | Primary    | Only on controller’s instructions |
| Ultimate liability                  | High       | Lower, but joint & several in some cases |

In practice, many organisations act as both controller and processor depending on the processing activity. The contractual allocation of responsibilities in the Art. 28 agreement is therefore critical.
